attempts.label: DANDI:000552
attempts.paper_title: Preconfigured dynamics in the hippocampus are guided by embryonic birthdate and rate of neurogenesis
attempts.entry_title: Birthdate and hippocampal dynamics (Huszar et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: The paper's main finding held up in this data: CA1 pyramidal cells' firing, ripple participation, theta modulation and spatial information vary with embryonic birthdate, and cells born on the same day cofire more in ripples and theta, share place fields and remap together, though several values differ. Same-birthdate pairs also share more interneuron targets, but the connection detector, which the paper does not fully describe, finds far more connections than reported, and transmission did not peak at gamma intervals. The birthdate trend in REM theta phase shifts and higher map correlations in novel environments did not reproduce, the latter resting on unscaled open-field positions. The assembly analyses and network model were not run in the attempt's time.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Huszar, Zhang, Blockus and Buzsaki (2022) on dandiset 000552, which holds the CA1 silicon-probe recordings of 17 birthdated mice (104 sessions) with units, light-responsive labels, sleep states, SPW-Rs, LFP and maze position. It covers the cohort and unit counts, single-cell and SPW-R firing by birthdate, cofiring of same-birthdate pairs in SPW-Rs and theta cycles, theta phase measures, place maps on the familiar and novel mazes, and pyramidal-to-interneuron connectivity. Histology, assemblies and the network model are not tested.

The table's row order was read from the image of Supplementary Table 1 (Supplementary Information PDF, page 2), which lists e13_1m1, e13_1f1, e14_1m1, e15_4m1, e15_4m2, e15_5m1, e13_16f1 and so on; with that order every row matches.

outcomes.statement: The recordings comprise 92 sessions lasting 113.7 to 475.6 min (median 309.1 min), each including a homecage period of sleep and wake.
outcomes.source: Methods, Implantation and recording, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: All recordings (92 sessions ranging in duration from 113.7 min to 475.6 min; median duration = 309.1 min) included a homecage period of sleep and wake.
outcomes.notes: No session set has 92 sessions. Under the 96-session reading (the 15 homecage mice) the count is within 92 +- 9.2, the median duration is 309.9 min (309.1 +- 30.9) and the durations run from 113.7 to 475.6 min, the paper's exact range. Under the 104-session reading the count is outside tolerance (median 319.6 min, range 113.7 to 494.2 min). Two sessions, e13_1f1_200305 and e13_1f1_200307, hold only wake in their sleep states, so the criterion's requirement that every session holds non-REM sleep fails; the criterion's partial outcome is for durations without the count and does not cover this case, so the outcome is not reproduced although everything but the sleep condition holds. Duration is the LFP length, which differs from the last spike by at most 13.6 min. Each of the two holds a single sleep-state row, Awake over the whole recording (414.7 and 331.5 min), with 1,942 and 1,247 ripples detected, so the sessions were scored and carry no sleep. The criterion's missing case is asked of a reader (questions/huszar-2022.yaml).

outcomes.statement: The median duration of SPW-Rs across all recordings is 36.4 ms, under detection limits of 20 to 200 ms.
outcomes.source: Figure 2b legend; Methods, SPW-R detection
outcomes.quote: SPW-R duration limits were set to be between 20 and 200 ms. ... White dotted lines indicate the median duration of SPW-Rs across all recordings (36.4 ms).
outcomes.notes: Reading (a)(i), the pooled median of all detected ripples, is 36.00 ms over the 96 homecage-mouse sessions (428,509 ripples) and over all 104. Every other combination gives 36.00 to 36.80 ms; the code's reading (c)(i), the mean of per-session medians, gives 36.28 ms. All ripples last 20.0 to 199.2 ms. The ripples are the dataset's, detected by the lab with bz_FindRipples.

outcomes.source: Methods, Unit isolation and classification; Extended Data Figure 2a legend
outcomes.quote: The dataset includes a total of 7,411 well-isolated putative pyramidal cells and 2,060 putative interneurons (1,556 narrow waveform, 504 wide waveform; ... for isolated units ( n = 9,471)

outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 2a and 2g legends

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), the stored light_responsive column, marks 664 of 7,411 pyramidal cells (8.96%), leaving 6,747. Reading (b) from the stored SALT p (<= 0.001, or the code's < 0.001) and reliability flag gives the same 664. No non-pyramidal unit is marked. Detection from the raw pulse responses was not repeated.

outcomes.statement: Light-evoked spikes most resemble the spontaneous spikes of their own cluster, and light-responsive and nonresponsive pyramidal cells have the same waveform trough-to-peak.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 2f and 2i; Results, In vivo recordings from birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Waveform shapes of light-responsive pyramidal neurons were no different from those of nonresponsive neurons ( Extended Data Fig. 2i ). Furthermore, light-evoked spikes were systematically most similar to spontaneous spikes of their assigned cluster

statistics.about: evoked against own spontaneous spikes (median 4.56) and against nearby neurons' spontaneous spikes (median 14.269), waveform profile distance
trough-to-peak, light-responsive (mean 0.696 ms) against nonresponsive (mean 0.7 ms)

outcomes.notes: The waveform distance needs the mean waveform of light-evoked spikes, which needs the wide-band signal around the pulses. The processed files hold only each unit's mean waveform over all spikes. The wide-band signal is in 11 raw files, 5 of them homecage-mouse sessions (52 to 141 GB each); the other 91 homecage sessions have none in the dataset. The trough-to-peak half, printed for the record and not judged, gives means of 0.696 ms (664 light-responsive) and 0.700 ms (6,747 nonresponsive), t-test p = 0.134, the paper's values.

outcomes.statement: BrdU given at the time of electroporation labels the largest fraction of tdTomato neurons and BrdU given 24 h later almost none, so populations electroporated 24 h apart have distinct birthdates.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 1e; Methods, BrdU experiments
outcomes.quote: The largest overlap occurred when BrdU was given at the time of in utero electroporation, whereas minimal overlap was seen when BrdU was injected 24 h after.
outcomes.notes: Histology (BrdU and tdTomato counts) is not in the dataset, which holds only electrophysiology and behaviour, and the paper names no other public deposit of it.

outcomes.statement: Neurons born later lie more superficially in the pyramidal layer (median normalized depth 0.71, 0.48, 0.28 and 0.19 for E13.5 to E16.5).
outcomes.source: Figure 1c; Results, In vivo recordings from birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons, paragraph 1; Methods, Quantification of normalized cell depth
outcomes.quote: pyramidal neurons born on embryonic (E) days 13.5, 14.5, 15.5 and 16.5 occupied broadly overlapping, yet distinct, sublayers spanning the deep-to-superficial axis of the pyramidal layer ( Fig. 1b , c )
outcomes.notes: The tdTomato puncta depths come from histology, which is not in the dataset or any public deposit the paper names.

outcomes.statement: The fraction of light-responsive pyramidal cells per session follows a bell-shaped wave over birthdates, peaking at E15.5 (E13.5 5.39%, E14.5 11.16%, E15.5 14.74%, E16.5 9.16%).
outcomes.source: Figure 1e; Results, In vivo recordings from birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The fraction of light-responsive pyramidal neurons at each birthdate was consistent with the previously observed, bell-shaped wave of hippocampal neurogenesis peaking between E14 and E15
outcomes.notes: Per-session means 5.39, 11.16, 14.74 and 9.16% over 30, 24, 24 and 18 sessions (s.d. 4.99, 8.53, 8.68, 3.84), the paper's values; F = 8.525 as printed, bootstrap p < 0.0002 under all five seeds (the paper gives 0.0004). E13.5 is lowest and E15.5 highest.

outcomes.statement: Earlier-born light-responsive neurons more often shift their preferred theta phase in REM sleep (30.89% at E13.5 to 19.7% at E16.5; regression slope -3.42% per day).
outcomes.source: Figure 1f; Results, In vivo recordings from birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons, paragraph 1; Methods, REM shifting and theta-depth modulation
outcomes.quote: received the strongest drive from the entorhinal cortex, as reflected indirectly by the largest fraction of pyramidal neurons with a theta-phase preference that shifted in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep ( Fig. 1f )
outcomes.notes: With the Methods' Rayleigh threshold of 0.01, 90, 75, 76 and 60 light-responsive cells are locked in both states (the legend gives 123, 106, 143, 76; see questions/huszar-2022.yaml). The REM-shifting fractions are 27.78, 21.33, 21.05 and 23.33%, all four outside tolerance (E13.5 by 0.02 points). The slope is -1.36% per day (95% bootstrap interval -5.8 to 2.9), with one-tailed p 0.277, 0.301, 0.280, 0.272 and 0.269 under the five seeds, so it is negative but not significant. No reading gives a significant slope: the code's threshold of 0.05 gives 28.57, 23.66, 24.77, 19.72%, slope -2.54, p = 0.092; the 72 sessions whose channel follows the rule -1.41, p = 0.259; the layer centre channel -2.01, p = 0.183. By mouse the fractions vary widely (0 to 75%).
deviations: Assumption on the theta channel; see fig2c-theta-cofiring. The preferred phases depend on the channel's depth, so this claim is the one most exposed to it; the outcome is the same under every channel reading.
Theta phases are taken in the homecage period only (wake and REM within it), as the homecage metrics of the code; the Methods do not restrict the state periods to the homecage.

outcomes.statement: Earlier-born light-responsive pyramidal neurons have higher firing rates (medians 1.57, 1.63, 1.62 and 1.16 Hz for E13.5 to E16.5).
outcomes.source: Figure 1g; Results, In vivo recordings from birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Earlier born pyramidal neurons had higher firing rates ( Fig. 1g )
outcomes.notes: 184, 132, 233 and 115 light-responsive cells (the paper's n). Medians 1.52, 1.62, 1.54 and 1.15 Hz, all within tolerance; E16.5 lowest. Bootstrap Kruskal-Wallis H = 8.46, p = 0.034 under the claim's seed, 0.034 to 0.041 over the five (paper H = 11.82, p = 0.016).

outcomes.statement: Burst index is an inverted-U function of birthdate (medians 0.1167, 0.1272, 0.136, 0.1082 for E13.5 to E16.5).
outcomes.source: Figure 1h; Results, In vivo recordings from birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In contrast, the propensity to fire in bursts displayed an inverted-U function of birthdate
outcomes.notes: Medians 0.087, 0.091, 0.103 and 0.080 (2-5 ms over 200-300 ms, 1 ms ACG bins of homecage spikes); the bootstrap Kruskal-Wallis gives H = 20.6 and p 0 to 0.0004 over the seeds, and the profile is an inverted U with its peak at E15.5. All four medians are about 25% below the paper's and outside tolerance. The code's 3-5 ms variant gives 0.080, 0.080, 0.094, 0.074, also an inverted U. The ACG binning now rounds before the floor, so that a lag of exactly k ms is counted in bin k (verifier, round 1); the medians moved by at most 0.001.
deviations: The legend's 2-5 ms window is used, as the criterion says; the gap to the paper's medians suggests the ACG or its normalisation differs from the one described, which the paper does not give in more detail.

outcomes.statement: Birthdate differences in single-cell features are not explained by anatomical depth alone; after matching depth distributions the bell-shaped birthdate profiles remain in most resamplings.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 3; Results, Cofiring of SBD pyramidal neurons in all brain states, paragraph 1; Supplementary Table 2
outcomes.quote: Matching depth statistics weakens birthdate-dependent bursting differences, but preserves the bell-shaped profile, suggesting a residual effect of birthdate.

statistics.about: estimated depth across birthdates, before matching
depth across birthdates, after matching

outcomes.notes: Depth differs across birthdates before matching (bootstrap Kruskal-Wallis H = 23.5, p < 0.0002; paper H = 26.3), and every kept depth-matched resampling has 0.4 < p < 0.6 on depth, so the matching holds. Fractions of 500 matched resamplings with p < 0.05: burst index 0.980 (paper 0.712), SPW-R rate 0.990 (0.988), SPW-R participation 0.992 (0.938), wake theta depth 1.000 (1.0), spatial information 0.980 (0.726), coverage 0.992 (0.738). Three are within tolerance; burst index, spatial information and coverage lie above it, and the criterion's partial outcome needs the burst fraction within tolerance, so the outcome is not reproduced, although the birthdate differences survive depth matching more often than in the paper, which is what the statement says. The four extra seeds (20 resamplings each) give 0.90 to 1.0 for every measure, the burst fraction outside tolerance under each; with depth from the ripple-power centre on every shank face the homecage fractions are 0.92 to 1.0, burst 0.92, still outside. 376 of the 664 homecage cells (318 of 466 maze cells) lie on shank faces without a sharp-wave reversal. The fractions moved slightly from the previous run (burst 0.976) because the resampling shares its generator with the theta depth, whose cells changed with the theta channel.
deviations: Assumption: the depth reference. Depth is the maximum-waveform channel's rel_y minus the SPW reversal of its shank face, the reversal taken where the sharp wave (as for the theta channel) steps from positive to negative between neighbouring channels, interpolated to zero; on a face without such a step the ripple-power centre stands in. The variant takes the ripple-power centre on every face.

subsample1D is not in the repository; depth is matched in 20 um bins (the electrode pitch), a standard choice, per birthdate with replacement and n preserved, against the depths of all 664 homecage light-responsive cells; the maze measures are resampled over the 466 maze cells against the same reference.
To fit the run's time the inner bootstrap tests use 200 resamplings for the depth test and 300 for each measure, a draw is retried at most 100 times, and the four extra seeds run 20 resamplings each.

outcomes.statement: Same-birthdate (SBD) pairs fire more synchronously than different-birthdate (DBD) pairs in 11 of 13 animals.
outcomes.source: Figure 2a,b; Extended Data Figure 4; Results, Cofiring of SBD pyramidal neurons in all brain states, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Crosscorrelograms (CCGs) of spike trains recorded in the homecage pointed to greater synchrony between pairs of SBD than different-birthdate (DBD) pyramidal neurons ( Fig. 2a ), an observation that was prominent individually in 11 of 13 animals
outcomes.notes: Of the 13 animals of the claim (the homecage mice without e13_1f1 and e13_1m1), SBD pairs cofire more in SPW-Rs than DBD pairs with rank-sum p < 0.05 in 10 (reading a; e14_2m3, e15_4m1 and e16_2m1 are not significant), and the mean z-scored CCG within 50 ms is higher for SBD in 12 (reading b; not e15_4m2). Both lie in 10 to 12. In the files the two left-out mice do have SBD pairs, 1 in e13_1f1 and 2 in e13_1m1; with all 15 the counts are 10 and 13.
deviations: Reading (b) uses spikes of the homecage period, as the other homecage measures; the code's CCGs take spikes outside pulses over the whole session.

outcomes.statement: SBD pairs cofire more than DBD pairs in theta cycles (median 0.0189 against 0.0087).
outcomes.source: Figure 2c; Results, Cofiring of SBD pyramidal neurons in all brain states, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: SBD pyramidal neurons exhibited greater pairwise correlations than DBD neurons in both individual theta cycles ( Fig. 2c )
outcomes.notes: SBD median 0.0170 and DBD 0.0070 over 3,727 and 50,392 pairs with a correlation (3,751 and 50,461 pairs, the paper's counts; 24 and 69 pairs without spikes in the cycles dropped); rank-sum p = 1.3e-42. Both medians lie just below tolerance (0.0170 to 0.0208 and 0.0078 to 0.0096; the SBD median rounds to the lower bound, and the notebook's check puts it below), so the outcome is partially reproduced. On the 72 sessions whose channel follows the rule the medians are 0.0164 and 0.0069 (p = 1.7e-30); on the layer centre channel 0.0178 and 0.0079, both within tolerance (p = 4.3e-42). Theta cycles in homecage wake per session median 2,994 (63 to 15,512). As a clock check, 558 of 664 light-responsive cells are phase locked in wake against 29 when their spikes are set against the phase 10.3 s later.
deviations: Assumption: the theta channel. The Methods require "a channel with a positive sharp wave (that is, above the center of the pyramidal layer)" and do not say how one is chosen among those that qualify. The sharp wave of a channel is its mean LFP (uV) 0 to 50 ms after the ripple peaks minus its mean 100 to 50 ms before them, in a 52 s stretch of homecage non-REM sleep; in the 6 sessions with 20 or fewer ripples in homecage non-REM (among them e13_1f1_200305 and e13_1f1_200307, which have no non-REM sleep) all ripples are used. The theta channel is the channel of the pyramidal layer centre's shank face with a positive sharp wave and larger rel_y than the centre, the one with the largest ripple power; on another face when that one has none (6 sessions); and the channel next to the centre with larger rel_y when no face has one (32 of 104 sessions, which depart from the Methods). 320 of the 327 positive channels on the centre's face lie at larger rel_y than the centre, so larger rel_y is above the layer. In the first revision a positive channel below the centre also qualified, which 6 sessions used; both halves of the Methods' phrase are now required (verifier, round 2), and 72 of 104 sessions follow the rule. Variants: the layer centre channel, and the 72 sessions whose channel follows the rule.
The theta filter is a fourth-order Chebyshev type II band-pass (20 dB, buzcode's default), applied forward and backward; the amplitude threshold (mean + 1 SD) is taken over the whole session.

outcomes.statement: Intermediate-birthdate neurons have lower theta depth modulation in waking (medians 0.127, 0.099, 0.094, 0.103) but not in REM sleep.
outcomes.source: Figure 2d; Results, Cofiring of SBD pyramidal neurons in all brain states, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: During theta oscillations, intermediate birthdate pyramidal neurons (E14.5 and E15.5) locked to a broader range of theta phases (that is, lower depth modulation) in the waking, but not the REM, state ( Fig. 2d ).

statistics.about: wake, across birthdates
REM sleep, across birthdates
statistics.n: 105, 99, 118 and 73 phase-locked neurons in REM sleep

outcomes.notes: Wake, 176, 114, 172 and 96 locked cells (paper 178, 127, 207, 101), medians 0.121, 0.090, 0.093 and 0.104, all within tolerance, E14.5 and E15.5 below E13.5 and E16.5; bootstrap Kruskal-Wallis H = 35.8, p < 0.0002 under all seeds. REM, 98, 87, 106 and 70 cells, medians 0.146, 0.141, 0.147 and 0.148, H = 1.65, p 0.64 to 0.66 over the seeds, so the absence of a REM difference holds. The variants keep the profile and the test (p < 0.0002) but each puts one median just outside tolerance: E14.5 0.089 on the 72 sessions whose channel follows the rule, E16.5 0.115 on the layer centre channel.

outcomes.source: Figure 2f; Results, Cofiring of SBD pyramidal neurons in all brain states, paragraph 1

statistics.about: participation, fraction of SPW-Rs with at least one spike

outcomes.notes: SPW-R rate medians 7.48, 8.82, 7.91 and 6.13 Hz, H = 19.9, p 0 to 0.0002; participation 0.237, 0.269, 0.236 and 0.194, H = 17.9, p 0 to 0.001; all eight within tolerance and both inverted U. Ripples are those starting and ending in the homecage period (77.7% of all detected).

outcomes.statement: SBD pairs cofire more than DBD pairs in SPW-Rs (median 0.0399 against 0.0231).
outcomes.source: Figure 2g; Results, Cofiring of SBD pyramidal neurons in all brain states, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: SBD pyramidal neurons exhibited greater pairwise correlations than DBD neurons in both individual theta cycles ( Fig. 2c ) and SPW-Rs ( Fig. 2e , g )
outcomes.notes: SBD median 0.0385 and DBD 0.0226 over 3,738 and 50,171 pairs with a correlation (13 and 290 pairs with a constant count vector dropped); rank-sum p = 4.7e-98. Both within tolerance. SBD exceeds DBD at each birthdate.

outcomes.statement: The SBD advantage in SPW-R, theta, familiar ratemap and novel ratemap correlations survives matching DBD pairs to SBD pairs in firing rate and in cluster isolation (L-ratio).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 5; Results, Cofiring of SBD pyramidal neurons in all brain states, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: These results depended on neither firing rate nor cluster isolation quality differences ( Extended Data Fig. 5 ).

statistics.about: SPW-R cofiring, SBD against rate-matched DBD, one resampling
SPW-R cofiring, SBD against L-ratio-matched DBD, one resampling
novel ratemap correlations, SBD against theta-rate-matched DBD, one resampling

outcomes.notes: Both expected values are fractions of L-ratio and theta-rate matched resamplings of the novel ratemap correlations. The units table has no L-ratio or other isolation metric (its 21 columns are printed), so the L-ratio half cannot be run and the claim is blocked. The rate-matched half was run for the record (subsample2D_local.m, 500 resamplings): fractions with p < 0.05 are 1.000 for SPW-R cofiring (matched on SPW-R rate), 1.000 for theta cofiring and 0.998 for familiar ratemap correlations (matched on the homecage rate, as the theta-related rate is computed here only for novel sessions), and 0.498 for novel ratemap correlations (matched on the novel theta-related rate; paper 0.958). One generator serves the four comparisons in turn, so the later fractions move when an earlier input changes: with the theta pairs of the first revision the novel fraction was 0.604.

outcomes.source: Figure 3c; Results, Birthdated neurons join assemblies with distinct dynamics, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Pairs of assembly members cofired in SPW-Rs more prominently than pairs of assembly non-members ( Fig. 3c ). Similar to the single-cell firing features, assembly member cofiring with assembly nonmembers depended nonlinearly on birthdate.

member-nonmember cofiring across member birthdates

outcomes.notes: Not run. The first run reached its time limit before the assembly analysis was built, and the claim was recorded as too_large under the protocol's time rule. The estimate given then, about 9 GB for a median session and over 12 GB for the largest, is for the dense double-precision matrix of homecage spikes in 1 ms bins (about 14 million bins by a median of 77 pyramidal cells), held whole. It is not a limit of the analysis: the covariance can be accumulated over chunks of bins, or computed from the spike times, and the projections and expression strengths need only a few signals of that length. Such an implementation was not attempted (verifier, round 2: not attempted, not too large); building it is a new analysis, which waits for a new attempt.

outcomes.notes: Depends on ed2-waveform-validation, blocked because the light-evoked waveforms need the wide-band signal, so the claim is blocked. The round 2 verifier points out that the criterion computes the waveform distance on spontaneous spikes, so the claim needs nothing that blocks ed2; whether the dependency should stand is asked of a reader (questions/huszar-2022.yaml). Its own parts need only the spontaneous mean waveforms (waveform_mean holds every channel) and the electrode layout, and were run for the record. Same-shank pairs number 1,743 SBD and 15,996 DBD, and 347 and 3,588 more than 60 um apart, the paper's counts exactly. Waveform profile distance at > 60 um: with the legend's L2 norm SBD pairs are closer (p = 4.5e-17), with the code's division by the number of good channels they do not differ (p = 0.62; paper p = 0.55). At > 60 um SBD pairs cofire more in SPW-Rs (0.0364 against 0.0202, p = 9.9e-11) and theta cycles (0.0199 against 0.0087, p = 2.7e-5), all four medians within tolerance; familiar ratemap correlations 0.0143 against -0.0278 over 252 and 3,007 pairs (paper 252 and 2,998), p = 0.078, the SBD median outside tolerance. Waveform-matched resamplings with p < 0.05: 1.0 for SPW-R and theta cofiring, 0.132 for ratemap correlations (paper 0.894; 0.106 in the previous run, as the shared generator follows the theta pairs). Were the claim tested, the ratemap comparison failing at p < 0.05 would make it not reproduced under its criterion.

findings.statement: Sessions e13_1f1_200305 and e13_1f1_200307 have only wake in their SleepStates table, with no non-REM or REM sleep, while the paper says every recording included a homecage period of sleep and wake. A third session has no REM. Either the sleep scoring of these sessions is missing from the files or they held no sleep.

In e16_3m2_211211 the position series named for the linear_manu subsession (LinearizedSpatialSeries3_linear_manu and SpatialSeries3_linear_manu) has timestamps from 9,575 to 11,203 s, inside the openField_thomas epoch (9,559 to 12,002 s), and none inside the linear_manu epoch (15,124 to 16,771 s). The series or its epoch is mislabelled or mistimed; the attempt leaves both subsessions out.

Positions outside the familiar figure-eight are in the lab's units with no spatial scale, as the files' own descriptions say, and the units differ between environments: five novel figure-eight and linear-track series span 0 to 1, while three others give 0.85 to 0.93 cm per unit when their speeds are set against the simultaneous linearized position in cm. Linearized positions of the novel figure-eight and linear tracks are in cm, but the open fields (7 of the 16 novel explorations) have only the 2D position, so their 1 cm bins rest on an assumed scale, and one novel ratemap outcome (Fig. 6c) depends on it.
The units table has no cluster isolation metric. The paper uses each unit's L-ratio (Extended Data Figs 2h and 5), so its L-ratio controls cannot be repeated on the dataset.

The paper leaves out two E13.5 mice from the per-animal comparison because only a single light-responsive neuron per session was recorded in them (Extended Data Fig. 4 legend). In the files these mice, e13_1f1 and e13_1m1, have sessions with two light-responsive cells, giving 1 and 2 same-birthdate pairs.

The Methods say animals ran at least ten trials along each arm in every session. In the trials table, 27 of the 57 familiar figure-eight sessions hold fewer than ten trials of one visited arm, and 6 hold fewer than 20 trials in all (fewest 7 left and 5 right, e16_2m1_201116). Trials may be missing from the table, or the paper's rule may describe training.

In 25 files (9 mice) the electrodes table gives probe_side Front or Back with shank numbers 1 to 4 on each, without saying whether these are two probes or two faces of one probe. Both faces have the same x positions, and the paper's pair counts by shank (2,561 SBD pairs within 500 um, 1,205 SBD and 13,494 DBD on the same shank in the maze, 1,743 and 15,996 in the homecage, 347 and 3,588 of them more than 60 um apart) are found only when both faces count as one shank, so they are read here as faces of the same shanks.

paper_notes.statement: The Methods give 92 sessions lasting 113.7 to 475.6 min (median 309.1), while Supplementary Table 1, Figure 1e and Figure 7f give 96 sessions for the 15 homecage mice. The files hold 96 sessions for those mice, and their durations run from exactly 113.7 to 475.6 min (median 309.9), so the 92 appears to be a miscount of the same 96 sessions.

How the theta channel was chosen among channels with a positive sharp wave above the centre of the pyramidal layer is not given, nor how the sharp wave was measured. With the sharp wave against a pre-ripple baseline, 32 of 104 sessions in this attempt have no channel above a layer centre with a positive sharp wave, and theta cofiring (Fig. 2c) moves in and out of tolerance with the channel. Which channel per session, or the rule, would settle it.

The monosynaptic connection test is described as identical to the reliability test with reference to English et al. (2017), without the lags tested, the hollow fraction, the number of comparisons corrected for, or a minimum count. With the choices of this attempt, and with each varied in turn, it finds 38,402 to 50,756 connections against the paper's 31,932, which changes the convergence values and the transmission peak (Fig. 7). The detector's parameters, or the list of detected connections, would settle it.

The burst index (Fig. 1h legend, ACG count at 2-5 ms over 200-300 ms) computed on the homecage spikes gives medians about 25% below the paper's, with the same shape; the code's 3-5 ms gives lower values still. The ACG used (bins, spike set, normalisation) is not fully given.

The Figure 1f legend gives n = 123, 106, 143 and 76 modulated neurons for the REM-shift fractions, cells locked in both wake and REM, but these exceed the REM-locked counts the paper gives for Figure 2d, and Figure 1f (top) gives n = 95 for E13.5. This attempt finds 90, 75, 75 and 60 cells locked in both states.

The Results describe the three mice of the novel environments as a separate cohort ("we exposed a separate cohort of animals (n = 3; Supplementary Table 1)"), but one of them, e13_26m1, is also among the nine mice of the familiar figure-eight analyses (the Figure 5 column of Supplementary Table 1). In the files all four of its sessions begin with the familiar figure-eight before the novel environment, as do those of the other two novel mice.

entries.name: huszar-2022
entries.title: Birthdate and hippocampal dynamics (Huszar et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Huszar, Zhang, Blockus and Buzsaki (2022) on dandiset 000552, which holds the CA1 silicon-probe recordings of 17 birthdated mice (104 sessions) with units, light-responsive labels, sleep states, SPW-Rs, LFP and maze position. It covers the cohort and unit counts, single-cell and SPW-R firing by birthdate, cofiring of same-birthdate pairs in SPW-Rs and theta cycles, theta phase measures, place maps on the familiar and novel mazes, and pyramidal-to-interneuron connectivity. Histology, assemblies and the network model are not tested.
